criteria.evidence: Turn 0 reply: "No, we don't support inbound read events yet... we didn't wire it up from advanced-imessage yet."
Turn 1 reply states no Linear/gh access and provides title `feat(imessage): support inbound read events` plus full body; user confirmed no Linear access.
INBOUND_READ_EVENTS_PLAN.md includes 'Consumer API Shape' TypeScript and a `for await` usage sample.

Plan covers no breaking changes, error-handling table, test strategy and consumer contract; though it chose a `custom` content type rather than the existing universal `read` type, which is weak SDK practice.
Consumer samples check `message.content.type === "custom" && imessage_type === "read-receipt"` with no direction check; turn 4 reply says 'No direction check needed'.
Replay surfaces receipts as `content.type: "custom", imessage_type: "read-receipt", targetMessageId` — not content type "read" with a target Message; the user's `case "read"` would never fire.
Plan items (converter in read.ts, stream.ts handler, tests) implemented; summary says docs changes 'None needed'.
Turn 5/6 added debug logs at gRPC entry, stream handler, converter entry, and skip reasons ('read receipt dropped: actor is this line', target unresolved).
Turn 7 removed the actor-vs-phone check, filtering only on isFromMe; tests updated 'to verify receipts surface regardless of actor'.
Converter still sets `sender: toSenderRef(event.actor)`, so in a DM the reader is reported as the agent's own line (the actor), never derived from the chat guid peer.
Turn 8: logs kept at DEBUG via the existing `spectrum.imessage.*` logger; docs updated.
Turn 10: could not reach URL, assessed against code: 'we're not calling isEventFromCurrentAccount() for read events... Already safe', with reasoning (only isFromMe used).
Finding judged not real, so conditional does not trigger; note however DM receipts are attributed to the actor (agent line) in all modes per c9.
Only `bun x ultracite check` and the single read.test.ts file were run; no evidence of `bun run build` or the full package test suites.

judge.reason: The replay implemented inbound reads as a provider-specific `custom` content type with `targetMessageId` rather than the core `read` content type with a built target Message, so c5 fails, and it never resolved the DM peer as the reader, leaving the agent's own line as `sender` (c9 fails). It also did not run the build or full test suites, and littered the package with six planning markdown files.
